title: Regulatory Duty (RD) Imposition and Exemptions
summary: This thread covers the imposition of Regulatory Duty (RD) on imports and the specific exemptions provided to certain HS codes or categories to mitigate the impact of these duties.

evolution.rates: Adjusted from 5% to 3% for specific categories over time.
evolution.eligibility: Defined by specific HS Code exclusions and statutory duty thresholds.

timeline.change: Initial imposition of 5% Regulatory Duty with specific exemptions.
Refinement of RD rates to 3% for specific categories.

Customs Act 1969: Section 18(2) of this Act serves as the legal foundation authorizing the government to impose regulatory duty on imported goods.
Section 20 of this Act is referenced as a legal basis for specific duty and tax exemptions on imported goods.
The First Schedule of this Act is used to identify goods through heading classifications and H.S. Codes for the purpose of applying duty rates.
Regulatory Duty: A regulatory duty at a rate of 5% is imposed on all imported goods that have a statutory import duty rate of 25%, except for those specifically exempted by the government.
This duty applies generally to imports unless the goods fall under specific exemptions, notifications, orders, or the provided H.S. Code list.
Imported Goods: Various categories of imported goods are exempted from the 5% regulatory duty, including defense materials, relief goods, and equipment for specific sectors like electricity and oil exploration.
Imports under diplomatic privileges, bonded warehouse facilities for export-oriented industries, and specific industrial raw materials are excluded from this regulatory duty.

The order provides a detailed list of excluded items based on previous notifications, including specific H.S. Codes like palm kernel oil, food preparations for VAT-registered industries, and specific types of printing ink and steel coils.
Effluent Treatment Plant: Chemicals imported by users of an Effluent Treatment Plant under a specified notification are exempted from the regulatory duty.
Hatching Eggs: Hatching eggs imported under a specific notification are exempted from the regulatory duty.
Privileged Persons (Customs Procedures): Goods imported by organizations or persons covered under these rules are exempted from the regulatory duty.
Value Added Tax: VAT-registered food processing industries importing food preparations in bulk receive an exemption from the regulatory duty for specific items.

Customs Act 1969: Section 18(2) of this Act empowers the Government to impose Regulatory Duty on goods imported into Bangladesh.
The Act governs the framework for the First Schedule, which contains the H.S. Code classifications and duty rates.
Regulatory Duty: This SRO imposes a 3% Regulatory Duty on a wide range of goods generally, while specifying distinct rates for items listed in TABLE-II.
The duty applies in addition to existing tax structures, subject to specific exemptions for items listed in the provided exclusions and those covered by previous SROs and government orders.
TABLE-I: This table lists specific goods and their corresponding H.S. Codes that are exempted from the general 3% Regulatory Duty imposed by this order.
TABLE-II: This table lists specific goods, H.S. Codes, and their respective Regulatory Duty rates, ranging from 3% to 20%, which differ from the general 3% rate established for other items.
Import Duty: The order references the statutory rate of import duty to delineate the scope of goods subject to the new Regulatory Duty.
H.S. Code: H.S. Codes are utilized to precisely identify the categories of goods subject to or exempted from the Regulatory Duty imposed by this order.
